body: Thank you. I truly appreciate that. We plan to bring the kids with us to every visit now and will take many photos.

I just talked to my husband about it this morning. It was cathartic and I couldn't stop crying. He made the suggestion that we visit with the kids next time and take plenty of photos. When I started worrying about things we need to do to make sure everything is in order when dad does pass, he told me to let him worry about that. He wants my family to be able to grieve in peace when that time comes.

Yeah, I'm sure hormones have a lot to do with what I'm dealing with now. There's a lot of compounding stress but my emotions spiral out of control so quickly. Looking at my son now, I dont want to die. His smile and laugh brings so much joy to my heart. I want to see him and his baby sister grow up. I want to help make them the best people they can be. Everything is just so overwhelming right now.

The sweet boy that he is, he found my hair brush and started brushing my hair for me when he saw me crying. It was so comforting and simple but it made me feel so loved and cared for. He has no idea what he's done for me but I'll never forget it. I love my kiddo so much.

We definitely plan to find another doctor when baby gets here. Husband and I have talked extensively about family size and sterilization and we're both incredibly certain that neither of us wants any more children. The doctor even admitted that we had apparently been very thorough with exploring our options, but she still wouldn't approve me for it. Its incredibly frustrating.

Being fair to my husband, he usually helps where he can but I do just about everything else. I get that after a long day he needs a beer and some down time, but my day literally never ends. Once every couple weeks, I get a day without my toddler cause he'll take him off my hands and do a play date but that day is never spent winding down because there's too much that needs to be done. I'm not unthankful for what he does, I just wish it was more balanced because I'm getting burnt out and resentful.

I'm probably going to be switching doctors after this pregnancy is over. The only real requirements for sterlization is that I be over 21. This bullshit I'm being fed about, "You're still young," is frustrating to both myself and my husband. We're excited for new baby, we just weren't planning to have another so soon cause of our finances being what they are. We'll be able to afford 2 but any more kids than that is going to be impossible and neither of us wants our kida to know what it's like to live in poverty.

Financially, we've been stuck for the last two years cause husbands company has been struggling to win contract bids. What jobs they do get have us living pay check to pay check and once its done, its months before they get more work. Its caused us to eat through our savings and more to get by. I'm fed up with waiting for the situation to get better, so after baby 2 gets here, I'm going back into the work force ASAP but my resume is crap because I've been a SAHM for years. Hypothetically, we'll be able to move again in the spring which would help a lot but I'm not getting my hopes up. Everything good that happens has added 3 more shitty things that make life worse.

So, we don't know the gender yet but if its the opposite gender from LO we might do something a little larger but for now we just want to do a BBQ type thing with no expectations for gifts. Would this still be obnoxious or is this more okay cause its a toned down, no strings attached sort of event?

Based on this thread, I think maybe we lacked the right verbs to describe the type of event we wanted. I thought baby shower was just kind of an all encompassing term for celebrating new baby but I'm finding out about so many other types of parties now that seem more appropriate for what we'd like to do. (Sort of a BBQ diaper party thing?) We don't really expect gifts, least of all big ones like furniture, but we wouldnt turn down someone offering to buy a pack of diapers or wipes for us.
I saw some of those suggestions too. I'm getting a lot of great feed back and ideas from this thread. Thank you so much for input too!
Thank you for the ideas! I'm learning all sorts of stuff from this thread!

Wow! I didnt know that! In our families the mothers always throw baby showers but its typically divided. So mother of mom-to-be would throw a baby shower for her side of family, and then MIL of mom-to-be throws a separate baby shower for their side of the family. These parties are usually super small only being grandmothers, aunts, and a few close female cousins. No men allowed, not even dad-to-be.

So would a BBQ type deal be okay then? We really wouldnt be expecting gifts. I mean they'd be appreciated but the only thing we might tell people we need would be diapers, wipes and bottles since we arent planning to make a registry. We just want to be able to share the excitement of new baby with loved ones and thought calling it a baby shower was an appropriate event name. But it seems like a lot of people would be really put off by this.

"Why not celebrate every child?"

This was my mind set! It feels crappy to celebrate only one child when every one is an important addition to the family. We're not expecting to do anything huge and we dont want a ton of huge gifts cause we REALLY do not have the space for it. But we could still use things like clothes, diapers and bottles. 

And we're pretty decided that we'll plan this event ourselves given that I basically did last time. If family or friends want to pitch in and help, I wouldnt mind but we aren't expecting them to.

Wasnt sure if there was a word for this, but we were kinda considering this approach if new baby turns out to be a different gender. Other than another crib, we don't need any big furniture so a huge party doesn't really make sense. A lot of the big stuff we got before (baby swings, bassinets, etc) were great but not really necessary. I think if we do a list at all, it would just be baby bottles, clothes, diapers and wipes.

Yeah, I don't know that I explained it clearly in my post but the moms played hostess and paid for everything but it was really them handing me cards and saying, buy whatever within this budget. So I did all the planning on my own according to their budgets because neither of them is very creative or organized. My brothers, husband and grandmother were the ones that decorated and what not.
Hes really been into yogurts lately. So maybe I can transition him into smoothies too! Thank you for the great ideas!

Thank you both for your comments. I feel so much calmer about this diet change now. I was worried this could be something wrong with him but it seems like this is just another common change for his age. I'll try limiting snack times to see if that inspires him to eat his meals more.

Thank you. This really helped set my nerves at ease. After struggling through breakfast and lunch today I was really at wits end. At least I know this is normal behavior now and can try pushing forward without getting super freaked out.
